title: How to Report Cyber Crime
description: Step-by-step guide to reporting cyber fraud, hacking, online harassment, and other cyber crimes in India.

steps.title: Document Everything
steps.description: Take screenshots of fraudulent messages, emails, transactions, and websites. Note down phone numbers, email addresses, and UPI IDs used by scammers. Save all evidence before it disappears.

steps.title: Call the Cyber Crime Helpline
steps.description: Call 1930 immediately. This is the national cyber crime helpline that operates 24/7. For financial fraud, calling within the "golden hour" (first few hours) significantly increases chances of recovery.

steps.title: File an Online Complaint
steps.description: Visit cybercrime.gov.in and register your complaint. Select the appropriate category (financial fraud, women/child-related, or other cyber crime). You will receive a complaint acknowledgment number.

steps.title: File an FIR
steps.description: Visit your nearest police station and file a First Information Report (FIR). You can file a Zero FIR at any police station regardless of where the crime occurred. Carry all your evidence and the online complaint number.

steps.title: Contact Your Bank
steps.description: If financial fraud is involved, immediately contact your bank's customer care. Request them to block the transaction if possible. Report the unauthorized transaction in writing and get an acknowledgment.

requiredDocuments: Scammer's phone number, email, UPI ID, or bank account
importantWarnings: Report financial fraud within 3 days for better chances of recovery
Do not delete any evidence — even if scammers ask you to
Police cannot refuse to file an FIR for cognizable offenses
Keep your complaint acknowledgment number safe for follow-up
followUpSteps: Track your complaint status on cybercrime.gov.in
Follow up with the investigating officer assigned to your case
If no action is taken within 30 days, escalate to the SP/DIG
You can approach the court directly if police do not act

title: How to File a Consumer Complaint
description: Guide to filing complaints about defective products, poor services, or unfair trade practices.

steps.title: Write to the Company
steps.description: Send a written complaint to the company/seller first. Use email or registered post. Give them 15-30 days to respond. Keep a copy of the complaint and delivery proof.

steps.title: Call National Consumer Helpline
steps.description: Call 1800-11-4000 (toll-free) for guidance and mediation. They can help resolve complaints through direct intervention with companies.

steps.title: File on e-Daakhil Portal
steps.description: If the company does not resolve your issue, file a formal complaint on edaakhil.nic.in. This is the official online consumer complaint filing system. Choose the appropriate Consumer Commission based on your claim value.

steps.title: Pay the Filing Fee
steps.description: Pay the applicable filing fee online. Fees vary based on claim amount — starting from ₹100 for claims up to ₹5 lakh. Fee is waived for certain categories.

steps.title: Attend the Hearing
steps.description: You will receive a hearing date. You can represent yourself or hire a lawyer. Present your evidence and arguments. Consumer courts typically resolve cases faster than civil courts.

requiredDocuments: Photos/videos of defective product or poor service
Written complaint sent to company and their response
importantWarnings: File within 2 years of the cause of complaint
Keep all original documents safe — courts may need originals
You do not need a lawyer for consumer court — you can argue yourself
District Commission handles claims up to ₹1 crore, State Commission up to ₹10 crore
followUpSteps: Track your case status on edaakhil.nic.in
Attend all hearings on scheduled dates
If dissatisfied with the order, appeal to the next higher commission
Consumer Commission orders are legally enforceable

title: How to File a Banking Complaint
description: Guide to resolving disputes with banks regarding unauthorized transactions, service issues, and loan problems.

steps.title: Complain to Your Bank
steps.description: File a written complaint with your bank's Grievance Redressal Officer. Every bank is required to acknowledge your complaint and assign a reference number. They must respond within 30 days.

steps.title: Escalate to Banking Ombudsman
steps.description: If the bank doesn't resolve your complaint in 30 days, file with the RBI Banking Ombudsman on cms.rbi.org.in. This is a free service.

steps.title: Submit Supporting Documents
steps.description: Upload all relevant documents — bank statements, transaction records, communication with bank, complaint acknowledgment, etc.

steps.title: Await Mediation/Resolution
steps.description: The Ombudsman will mediate between you and the bank. Most cases are resolved within 30-45 days. The Ombudsman can award compensation.

steps.title: Appeal if Unsatisfied
steps.description: If dissatisfied with the Ombudsman's decision, you can appeal to the RBI Deputy Governor. You can also approach the Consumer Forum or civil court.

requiredDocuments: Written complaint to bank and acknowledgment
Loan agreement or fixed deposit receipt (if applicable)
importantWarnings: For unauthorized electronic transactions, report to bank within 3 days for zero liability
Keep complaint reference numbers for tracking
Banks must credit the disputed amount within 10 days of receiving your complaint (as per RBI guidelines)
The Ombudsman service is completely free
followUpSteps: Track complaint status on cms.rbi.org.in
If the bank doesn't comply with the Ombudsman's order, report to RBI
Consider filing a consumer complaint for compensation beyond the disputed amount
Keep records of all interactions for future reference

title: How to File a Police Complaint (FIR)
description: Complete guide to filing an FIR, understanding your rights, and what to do if police refuse your complaint.

steps.title: Visit the Police Station
steps.description: Go to the nearest police station. For cognizable offenses (serious crimes like theft, assault, fraud), the police are legally bound to file an FIR. You can also file a Zero FIR at any police station regardless of jurisdiction.

steps.title: Provide Your Statement
steps.description: Clearly narrate what happened — include details like date, time, location, description of the accused, and what occurred. Be factual and include all relevant details.

steps.title: Get FIR Copy
steps.description: Once the FIR is registered, you have the RIGHT to a free copy of the FIR. The FIR number is important for all future reference and legal proceedings.

steps.title: If Police Refuse to File FIR
steps.description: If police refuse, you have options: (1) Send a written complaint by registered post to the SP/SSP, (2) File a private complaint before the Magistrate under Section 190 CrPC, (3) File a complaint with the Police Complaints Authority, (4) Approach the High Court.

steps.title: Follow Up
steps.description: Note the investigating officer's name and contact. Follow up regularly on the investigation status. You can check FIR status online in some states through the police department website.

requiredDocuments: Medical report (in case of physical assault)
Previous complaints (if any) related to the incident
importantWarnings: Police CANNOT refuse to file an FIR for a cognizable offense — it is a criminal offense to do so
You can file a Zero FIR at ANY police station
Women have the right to give statements at their place of choice
Free legal aid is available for economically weaker sections
Keep the FIR copy — it is your primary legal document
followUpSteps: Track investigation progress with the SHO/IO
If investigation is slow, write to the SP/DIG
You can approach the Magistrate for directions to the police
Consult a lawyer for serious cases

title: How to File a Government Complaint (CPGRAMS)
description: Guide to filing grievances against central government departments and officers.

steps.title: Register on CPGRAMS
steps.description: Visit pgportal.gov.in and create an account. CPGRAMS (Centralized Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System) handles complaints against all central government departments.

steps.title: Select the Right Department
steps.description: Choose the relevant ministry/department your complaint relates to. Be specific — selecting the right department ensures faster processing.

steps.title: Write Clear Complaint
steps.description: Describe your grievance clearly with dates, reference numbers, and specific issues. Attach supporting documents. Keep the complaint factual and concise.

steps.title: Track Progress
steps.description: You will receive a unique registration number. Use this to track your complaint status online. Departments are expected to respond within 60 days.

steps.title: Escalate if Needed
steps.description: If unsatisfied with the response, you can reopen the grievance or file an appeal. You can also write to the Cabinet Secretary or approach the Administrative Tribunal.

requiredDocuments: Government order/notification relevant to your issue
importantWarnings: CPGRAMS is for central government departments only — use state grievance portals for state matters
Anonymous complaints are generally not acted upon
File an RTI application if the department doesn't provide information you requested
Keep the registration number for tracking
followUpSteps: Check status regularly on pgportal.gov.in
If closed without resolution, file an appeal
Consider filing an RTI to understand why your complaint was closed
Approach the concerned parliamentary committee if needed

title: How to File a Workplace Complaint
description: Guide to addressing workplace issues including harassment, unpaid wages, and unfair treatment.

steps.title: Internal Complaint
steps.description: First, file a written complaint with your HR department or Internal Complaints Committee (ICC). For sexual harassment, every organization with 10+ employees must have an ICC. Document everything.

steps.title: Contact Labour Commissioner
steps.description: If internal resolution fails, approach the Labour Commissioner's office for issues like unpaid wages, illegal termination, or unsafe working conditions. File a written complaint with supporting documents.

steps.title: File on Shram Suvidha Portal
steps.description: For central government labor law violations, you can file complaints on shramsuvidha.gov.in. State labor departments also have their own portals.

steps.title: Seek Legal Aid
steps.description: Contact NALSA or your District Legal Services Authority for free legal aid. They can provide a lawyer to represent you in the Labour Court.

steps.title: Approach Labour Court
steps.description: For wrongful termination or major disputes, file a case before the Labour Court or Industrial Tribunal. Your lawyer or legal aid lawyer will guide the process.

requiredDocuments: Written complaint to employer and their response
Evidence of workplace issue (emails, messages, photos)
importantWarnings: Document all workplace issues from the beginning
Sexual harassment complaints must be filed within 3 months of the incident
You cannot be terminated for filing a complaint — retaliation is illegal
Labour laws apply even to contract/temporary workers
followUpSteps: Follow up with the ICC for harassment complaints (they must complete inquiry within 90 days)
Track your Labour Commissioner complaint
Attend all hearings at Labour Court
Keep records of any retaliation after filing complaint

title: How to Report Online Fraud
description: Quick guide to reporting online shopping fraud, e-commerce scams, and digital payment fraud.

steps.title: Report to the Platform
steps.description: First, report the issue to the e-commerce platform (Amazon, Flipkart, etc.) through their customer service. Request a refund or return. Keep the complaint reference number.

steps.title: Report Payment Fraud
steps.description: If money was fraudulently deducted, contact your bank/UPI provider immediately. For UPI fraud, raise a dispute in the UPI app. For credit card fraud, call the card issuer to block the card.

steps.title: File Cyber Crime Complaint
steps.description: Report on cybercrime.gov.in and call 1930. Provide transaction details, screenshots, and the seller's information.

steps.title: File Consumer Complaint
steps.description: If the e-commerce platform doesn't resolve the issue, file a consumer complaint on edaakhil.nic.in. E-commerce companies are liable under the Consumer Protection Act.

steps.title: File FIR if Necessary
steps.description: For large amounts or criminal fraud, file an FIR at your local police station. This provides legal backing for further investigation and recovery.

importantWarnings: Act quickly — report financial fraud within hours for best recovery chances
Don't agree to deals outside the official platform (direct transfers)
Screenshot everything before the seller removes the listing
Keep communication within the platform for evidence
followUpSteps: Track refund status on the platform
Follow up on cyber crime complaint status
If platform closes your case unfairly, escalate to CCPA or consumer forum
Review and warn others about the fraudulent seller

title: How to Report a Traffic Violation
description: Guide to reporting traffic violations, checking e-challans, and addressing traffic-related issues.

steps.title: Document the Violation
steps.description: Take a photo or video of the traffic violation including the vehicle number, date, time, and location. Dash cam footage is also acceptable evidence.

steps.title: Report Online
steps.description: Many states have online traffic violation reporting systems. You can also report via the traffic police's social media handles (Twitter/X is commonly used by traffic police).

steps.title: Use the Parivahan App
steps.description: Download the mParivahan app for checking vehicle details and reporting violations. You can also check your own e-challan status on echallan.parivahan.gov.in.

steps.title: Visit Traffic Police Station
steps.description: For serious violations or accidents, visit the nearest traffic police station. File a written complaint with evidence.

steps.title: Check & Pay E-Challans
steps.description: Regularly check for e-challans on echallan.parivahan.gov.in using your vehicle number. Pay legitimate challans online to avoid penalties.

importantWarnings: Only pay e-challans through official government portals
Do not pay fines to individuals claiming to be traffic police (unless in proper uniform with ID)
You have the right to see the challan receipt
Beware of fake e-challan SMS scams
followUpSteps: Track your complaint through the traffic police portal
If issued an unfair challan, file a dispute through the online portal
For accident-related complaints, follow up with the investigating officer
Approach the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal for accident compensation

title: How to File a Tax Complaint
description: Guide to addressing tax-related issues including refund delays, TDS disputes, and GST problems.

steps.title: Contact CPC/Assessing Officer
steps.description: For income tax issues, first contact the Centralized Processing Centre (CPC) or your jurisdictional Assessing Officer. Log into the Income Tax e-filing portal and raise a grievance.

steps.title: File Online Grievance
steps.description: Use the e-Nivaran facility on incometax.gov.in for income tax grievances. For GST issues, use the GST portal's grievance section.

steps.title: Escalate to Ombudsman
steps.description: If not resolved within 30 days, escalate to the Income Tax Ombudsman. The Ombudsman is an independent authority that handles taxpayer grievances.

steps.title: File CPC Grievance
steps.description: For refund-related issues, track your refund on the IT portal. If delayed beyond expected timelines, file a specific refund-related grievance.

steps.title: Approach ITAT
steps.description: For disputes with assessment orders, you can appeal to the Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals) and then to the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT).

importantWarnings: File returns and respond to notices within the deadline to avoid penalties
Keep all tax-related documents for at least 6 years
Never share your e-filing password with tax "consultants" you don't trust
Beware of fake income tax refund SMS/emails
followUpSteps: Track grievance status on the IT portal
Check refund status online
If assessment order is unfair, file appeal within 30 days
Consult a chartered accountant for complex tax disputes

title: How to Report Environmental Violations
description: Guide to reporting pollution, illegal construction, deforestation, and other environmental violations.

steps.title: Document the Violation
steps.description: Take photos and videos of the environmental violation. Note the location, date, time, and nature of the violation (air pollution, water contamination, illegal construction, noise pollution, deforestation, etc.).

steps.title: Report to Pollution Control Board
steps.description: File a complaint with your State Pollution Control Board (SPCB) or Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB). Many SPCBs have online complaint systems.

steps.title: File on CPGRAMS
steps.description: File a grievance on pgportal.gov.in addressed to the Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change.

steps.title: Approach NGT
steps.description: For serious environmental issues, file an application with the National Green Tribunal (NGT). You don't need a lawyer — individuals can file directly.

steps.title: Contact Local Authorities
steps.description: Report to the Municipal Corporation, District Collector, or Forest Department depending on the nature of the violation.

importantWarnings: Environmental protection is a fundamental right (Article 21)
You don't need to be directly affected to file an environmental complaint
NGT can award compensation and direct restoration
Document the impact on daily life and health
followUpSteps: Follow up with the Pollution Control Board
Track your NGT application status
If no action is taken, approach the High Court
Connect with local environmental organizations for support
